module_title: Extremist Phase (1905-1918) - Revolutionary Nationalism, Ghadar Movement, and Global Impact
introduction: This advanced level focuses on the analytical study of the first phase of 'Revolutionary Nationalism', freedom efforts organized outside India (Ghadar Party), the Komagata Maru incident, and the British government's 'August Declaration (1917)' amidst World War I.

core_concepts.title: Rise of Revolutionary Nationalism
core_concepts.description: To fill the political vacuum created by the decline of the Swadeshi movement and the arrest of Extremist leaders, youth turned to revolutionary terrorism (bombs and assassinations). 'Anushilan Samiti' and 'Yugantar' were key secret societies in Bengal.

core_concepts.title: Ghadar Party (1913)
core_concepts.description: Founded by Lala Hardayal and Sohan Singh Bhakna in San Francisco (USA) to overthrow British rule in India through an armed rebellion. They published a weekly paper called 'Ghadar'.

core_concepts.title: Komagata Maru Incident (1914)
core_concepts.description: Komagata Maru was a Japanese ship chartered by Baba Gurdit Singh. When the Canadian government denied entry to Indian passengers in Vancouver and forced them back, a deadly clash occurred with British police at Budge Budge (Calcutta). This highly inflamed the Ghadarites.

core_concepts.title: August Declaration (Montagu Declaration - 1917)
core_concepts.description: Secretary of State Edwin Montagu declared in the British Parliament that the goal of British policy was the gradual development of 'responsible government' in India. This declaration effectively slowed down the Home Rule movement.

core_concepts.title: British 'Carrot and Stick' Policy
core_concepts.description: The British used a dual strategy: offering reforms as a 'carrot' to pacify the Moderates (e.g., 1909 Act) while using severe repression (the 'stick') to crush the Extremists and Revolutionaries.

important_entities.name: Madam Bhikaji Cama
important_entities.significance: She unfurled the first version of the Indian national flag (green, yellow, and red) at the International Socialist Conference in Stuttgart, Germany in 1907.

important_entities.name: Rash Behari Bose
important_entities.significance: Masterminded the bomb attack on Viceroy Lord Hardinge in 1912. He later fled to Japan and played a crucial role in founding the Indian National Army (INA).

important_entities.name: Prafulla Chaki and Khudiram Bose
important_entities.significance: They threw a bomb at a carriage to assassinate the unpopular judge Kingsford. Khudiram Bose was hanged at the young age of 18.

trap_alerts_and_exceptions.explanation: The Ghadar Party was not founded in India. Its headquarters was the 'Yugantar Ashram' located in San Francisco, USA.

Do not confuse the two. The 'August Declaration' was made in 1917 by Montagu (promising responsible government), whereas the 'August Offer' was made in 1940 by Viceroy Linlithgow (offering Dominion Status during WWII).

mnemonics_and_tricks.explanation: A quick cheat sheet to directly memorize the most tested revolutionary publications from Bengal and their editors.

exam_strategy_tips: Match the Following questions frequently target overseas revolutionary organizations (e.g., Shyamji Krishna Varma's 'India House' in London) with their founders and locations.
The chronological order of repressive British acts passed between 1905 and 1918 (like the Seditious Meetings Act 1907, Press Act 1910) is a favorite topic in UPSC and State PCS exams.
